conflicts.point: Whether pre-deployment circuit-level interpretability audits reliably catch failure modes and improve clinical safety compared to retrospective empirical error-rate tracking.

positions.stance: Pre-deployment interpretability audits inspect internal feature representations directly, providing the necessary mechanism to detect hazardous activation patterns before clinical deployment.
Clinical software should be evaluated on empirical error rates and diagnostic accuracy in real-world workflows rather than unproven internal feature mappings.
Internal activation maps do not replace randomized trial validation measured against historical patient cohorts and actual diagnostic error rates.

conflicts.point: Whether compute thresholds such as 10^26 integer operations serve as a necessary safeguard against critical control failures or function as an arbitrary barrier that protects market incumbents.

positions.stance: Compute thresholds above 10^26 integer operations effectively isolate frontier models where uninterpretable reasoning traces pose systemic risks.
Compute ceilings and export controls on specialized silicon construct administrative moats that restrict access and stifle permissionless innovation.
Fixed compute ceilings are arbitrary metrics disconnected from actual clinical error rates or operational risks.

verdicts.conflict: Whether pre-deployment circuit-level interpretability audits reliably catch failure modes and improve clinical safety compared to retrospective empirical error-rate tracking.
verdicts.rationale: Neither side presents peer-reviewed data showing that circuit-level inspections outperform traditional clinical error tracking in hospital environments. Both claims rest on unproven methodologies without large-scale deployment records.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Published comparative studies showing that internal activation tracing detects novel failure modes faster than standard randomized controlled trials.

verdicts.conflict: Whether compute thresholds such as 10^26 integer operations serve as a necessary safeguard against critical control failures or function as an arbitrary barrier that protects market incumbents.
verdicts.rationale: Critics provide concrete evidence regarding how compliance costs burden independent developers more than large firms. Safety proponents rely on abstract risk models without specifying how fixed compute ceilings prevent systemic harm without locking in market concentration.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Empirical proof that fixed compute ceilings directly reduce systemic AI control failures without disproportionately harming small labs.
